questions.question: Simplify the following expression: 9991 x 10009
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the numbers as **10000 − 9** and **10000 + 9**.

Apply the **Difference of Squares** trick: 10000² − 9².

100000000 − 81 = 99999919.

**∴ The correct answer is 99999919.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 9991 × 10009

**Formula Used:** (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²

⇒ 9991 × 10009 = (10000 − 9) × (10000 + 9)

⇒ Here, **a = 10000** and **b = 9**

⇒ Calculation = 10000² − 9²

⇒ Calculation = 100,000,000 − 81

⇒ Result = 99999919

**∴ The correct answer is 99999919.**

**__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares

The algebraic identity (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b² is highly effective for multiplying two numbers that are equidistant from a round **base number**.

Base 10 Squaring

When squaring a number like 10ⁿ, the number of **zeros** in the result is exactly 2 × n (e.g., 100² = 10000).

BODMAS Rule

In complex **simplification**, always prioritize calculations in the order: Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.</p

questions.question: In two triangles ABC and DEF, if overline{AB} = overline{EF} , overline{BC} = overline{DF} and overline{CA} = overline{DE} , then:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the correct **congruence** relation, identify the **corresponding vertices** by looking at the shared sides.

Common vertex in AB and BC is **B**; common vertex in EF and DF is **F** ⇒ B corresponds to F.

Common vertex in BC and CA is **C**; common vertex in DF and DE is **D** ⇒ C corresponds to D.

Common vertex in CA and AB is **A**; common vertex in DE and EF is **E** ⇒ A corresponds to E.

Mapping vertices: C → D, B → F, A → E.

Arranging them in order gives **ΔCBA ≅ ΔDFE**.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔCBA ≅ ΔDFE.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

In **ΔABC** and **ΔDEF**:

AB = EF

BC = DF

CA = DE

**Formula Used:**

**SSS (Side-Side-Side) Congruence Rule:** Two triangles are congruent if all three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding three sides of the other triangle. The **order of vertices** must match the **equal sides**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c5ff9f1f554e5d1e59117137b8c9c97dc1508a3fbb75a3ec1d26a290a31e3fff.png] 

To establish the **symbolic form** of congruence, we match vertices based on the given side lengths:

⇒ Given AB = EF, the vertices A and B correspond to E and F.

⇒ Given BC = DF, the vertices B and C correspond to F and D.

⇒ Looking at both, the **common vertex** B in the first triangle matches the **common vertex** F in the second triangle ⇒ B ↔ F.

⇒ From BC = DF and B ↔ F, it follows that C ↔ D.

⇒ From AB = EF and B ↔ F, it follows that A ↔ E.

⇒ Therefore, vertex C matches D, vertex B matches F, and vertex A matches E.

⇒ Writing this in order: ΔCBA is congruent to ΔDFE.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔCBA ≅ ΔDFE.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

SSS Congruence Criterion

If three sides of one triangle are equal to the three sides of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent by SSS rule.

CPCT (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles)

Once two triangles are proven congruent, their corresponding angles and remaining sides are automatically equal.

Congruence Naming Convention

The order of vertices in a congruence statement must strictly follow the correspondence of equal sides and equal angles.</p

questions.question: P is 30% more efficient than Q. How much time will they, working together, take to complete a job that P alone could have done in 23 days?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **efficiency** P : Q = 130 : 100 = **13 : 10**.

**Total Work** = Efficiency of P × Time taken by P = 13 × 23.

**Combined Efficiency** of P and Q = 13 + 10 = **23**.

Time taken together = (13 × 23) ÷ 23 = **13 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Efficiency** of P is 30% more than Q. **Time** taken by P = 23 days.

⇒ Let **efficiency** of Q = 10 units/day.

⇒ **Efficiency** of P = 130% of 10 = 13 units/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = Efficiency of P × Days = 13 × 23 = 299 units.

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** (P + Q) = 13 + 10 = 23 units/day.

⇒ **Time taken together** = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 299 ÷ 23 = **13 days**.

Combined Work Formula

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy, not heat.
 
• Electric stoves, water heaters, and iron boxes use the heating effect of current to function.
 
• In electric stoves, the current passes through resistive heating elements, generating heat.
 
• Electric water heaters use heating elements that convert electrical energy into heat to warm water.
 
• Electric iron boxes have resistive elements that produce heat to iron clothes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Commonly used in household appliances like toasters, hair dryers, and space heaters.

• This is the process by which an electric current passes through a resistive material, causing it to heat up.
 
• It is widely used in various applications, including industrial heating and household appliances.
 
 
 
• **Electric Motors**
 
 
• They are used in a wide range of applications, from household appliances to industrial machinery.
 
• Electric motors work based on electromagnetic induction and do not primarily rely on the heating effect of current.

questions.question: The median of the observations 4, 14, 11, 8, 7, 8, 9, 12, 4 and 6 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange **observations** in **ascending order**: 4, 4, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14.

Total terms (n) = 10, which is an **even number**.

Identify the **middle two terms**: The 5th and 6th terms are both 8.

**Median** = (8 + 8) ÷ 2 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set = {4, 14, 11, 8, 7, 8, 9, 12, 4, 6}

**Formula Used:** For an **even number** of observations (n), Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3bb887fd0e2281c51c88fbe02f80f6ed50b0da18b0e9a4de691cfbe58b20855.png] 

⇒ Arranging observations in **ascending order**: 4, 4, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14

⇒ Total count (n) = 10

⇒ **Median** = (5th observation + 6th observation) ÷ 2

⇒ **Median** = (8 + 8) ÷ 2

⇒ **Median** = 16 ÷ 2 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Odd N

If the number of observations (n) is odd, the median is the exactly middle value: Median = ((n+1)/2)th term.

Arithmetic Mean

The average value calculated by summing all observations and dividing by the total count: Mean = (Σx) ÷ n.

Mode of Data

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in the data set. A set can be unimodal, bimodal, or multimodal.

Range

The difference between the maximum and minimum values in the data set: Range = Max − Min.</p

questions.question: Which of the following Acts was amended in 2023 to enhance child protection measures in India?

options.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 has been passed by the Parliament of India amidst intense controversy, debate, and protest on many of its provisions by the Child Rights fraternity.
 
• It replaced the Indian juvenile delinquency law, Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, and allows for juveniles in conflict with Law in the age group of 16–18, involved in Heinous Offences, to be tried as adults.
 
• The Act also sought to create a universally accessible adoption law for India, overtaking the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act (1956) (applicable to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, and Sikhs) and the Guardians and Wards Act (1890) (applicable to Muslims), though not replacing them.
 
• The Act came into Enforcement on 15 January 2016.
 
• It was passed on 7 May 2015 by the Lok Sabha amid intense protest by several Members of Parliament.
 
• It was passed on 22 December 2015 by the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Education Act**

 
 
• The RTE Act of the Parliament of India was enacted on 4 August 2009 and came into force on 1 April 2010. This act is also known as the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act because of its provision of, “the fundamental right of every child between the ages of 6 to 14 with specifies minimum norms in elementary schools.”
 
• Important Provisions of RTE are as follows:
 
• Right of children to free and compulsory education till completion of elementary education in a neighbourhood school.
 
• It makes provisions for a non-admitted child to be admitted to an age-appropriate class.
 
• It specifies the duties and responsibilities of appropriate Governments, local authority and parents in providing free and compulsory education.
 
• It lays down the norms and standards relating regarding Pupil Teacher Ratios (PTRs), buildings and infrastructure, school-working days, teacher-working hours.
 
• It provides for the appointment of appropriately trained teachers, i.e. teachers with the requisite entry and academic qualifications. 
 
• The act prohibits physical punishment and mental harassment.
 
• It provides for the development of curriculum in consonance with the values enshrined in the Constitution, and which would ensure the all-round development of the child. 
 
 
 
• **Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act**
 
 
• The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act was enacted in 1986. 
 
• It aims to prohibit the engagement of children in certain employments and regulate the conditions of work in others.
 
 
 
• **​Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act**
 
 
• To deal with child sexual abuse cases, the Government has brought in a special law, namely, The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.
 
• The Act has come into force with effect from 14th November 2012__ along with the Rules framed thereunder. 
 
• The POCSO Act, 2012 is a comprehensive law to provide for the protection of children from the offences of
 
 
• sexual assault
 
• sexual harassment
 
• pornography
 
 
 
• While safeguarding the interests of the child at every stage of the judicial process by incorporating child-friendly mechanisms for reporting, recording of evidence, investigation and speedy trial of offences through designated Special Courts.

questions.question: Umesh took 100 chocolates out of 250 chocolates from Ruchi. Umesh gave 20% of his chocolates to Shalaka and 35% of his chocolates to Marry. Then Ruchi gave 50% of her remaining chocolates to Umesh. Find the number of chocolates Umesh had at the end.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Umesh** left with: 100 × (100% − 20% − 35%) = 100 × 45% = 45.

**Ruchi** remaining: 250 − 100 = 150.

Transfer from **Ruchi**: 50% of 150 = 75.

Final count for **Umesh**: 45 + 75 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 chocolates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total chocolates = 250 | **Umesh** takes = 100 | **Ruchi** remaining = 150

**Umesh** gives away = 20% (to **Shalaka**) + 35% (to **Marry**) = 55%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d118223ecca99f45f085eb8e5a72ba1e77916fdd5e5c3ebdc95848707761c9b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Umesh** initial count = 100 chocolates

⇒ Chocolates given by **Umesh** = (20 + 35)% of 100 = 55% of 100 = 55

⇒ **Umesh** remaining count = 100 − 55 = 45

⇒ **Ruchi** initial remaining = 250 − 100 = 150

⇒ Chocolates given by **Ruchi** to **Umesh** = 50% of 150 = 75

⇒ Final chocolates with **Umesh** = 45 + 75 = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 120 chocolates.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Remaining

If a person spends x% and then y% of the **initial** amount, the remaining percentage is (100 − x − y)%.

Percentage of a Value

To find p% of a number N, use the formula: (p ÷ 100) × N.

Base Value Importance

Always identify the **correct base** for percentage calculations (e.g., 50% of **remaining** 150, not the original 250).</p

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct according to the law of conservation of mass?

options.text: Mass can be created but cannot be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can neither be created nor be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can be created in a chemical reaction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass can neither be created nor be destroyed in a chemical reaction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The law of conservation of mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• This principle was established by Antoine Lavoisier in the 18th century.
 
• In a closed system, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
 
• The law applies to both physical changes and chemical reactions.
 
• This law is fundamental to the field of chemistry and underpins stoichiometric calculations in chemical reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Definite Proportions**

 
 
• This law states that a chemical compound always contains the same proportion of elements by mass.
 
• It is also known as Proust's law.
 
 
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions**
 
 
• This law states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in ratios of small whole numbers.
 
• It was formulated by John Dalton.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry**
 
 
• It involves the calculation of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• It is based on the laws of conservation of mass and definite proportions.

questions.question: The number of chromosomes become half in a daughter cell by the process of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Meiosis is a type of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes of the parent cell.
 
• This process is essential for sexual reproduction and occurs in the germ cells to produce gametes (sperm and eggs).
 
• Meiosis involves two sequential divisions: meiosis I and meiosis II.
 
• During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes are separated, and during meiosis II, sister chromatids are separated.
 
• The reduction in chromosome number ensures that when fertilization occurs, the resulting zygote has the correct diploid number of chromosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Fission**

 
 
• Binary fission is a form of asexual reproduction commonly found in prokaryotes such as bacteria.
 
• During binary fission, the parent cell divides into two genetically identical daughter cells.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis**
 
 
• Mitosis is a type of cell division that results in two daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell.
 
• It is involved in growth, repair, and asexual reproduction in multicellular organisms.
 
 
 
• **Amitosis**
 
 
• Amitosis is a direct method of cell division where the nucleus and cytoplasm divide without the formation of chromosomes.
 
• This process is less common and occurs in some single-celled organisms and certain tissues.

questions.question: The weights (in kg) of 9 members of a school cricket team are 50, 63, x, 62, 64, 48, 51, 55, 48. If the mean weight is 56 kg, then the value of x is ________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of **deviations** from the **mean** is always **zero**.

Known deviations from 56: (50−56), (63−56), (62−56), (64−56), (48−56), (51−56), (55−56), (48−56)

⇒ −6, +7, +6, +8, −8, −5, −1, −8

Sum of known deviations = −7

For the total deviation to be zero, the deviation of **x** must be +7.

x = Mean + 7 = 56 + 7 = 63.

**∴ The correct answer is 63.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weights of 9 members = 50, 63, x, 62, 64, 48, 51, 55, 48 kg

Mean weight = 56 kg

Number of members (n) = 9

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d021a3f622ec615909566c64b0cab96e4a9fea907d56fe063832b788bcf4084.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Mean = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 56 = (50 + 63 + x + 62 + 64 + 48 + 51 + 55 + 48) ÷ 9

⇒ 56 × 9 = 441 + x

⇒ 504 = 441 + x

⇒ x = 504 − 441

⇒ x = 63

**∴ The correct answer is 63.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Arithmetic Mean

The sum of the **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero: Σ(xᵢ − Mean) = 0.

Effect of Changes

If every observation is **increased** or **decreased** by a constant k, the mean is also increased or decreased by k.

Combined Mean

If two groups have means M₁ and M₂ with sizes n₁ and n₂, the **combined mean** is (n₁M₁ + n₂M₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: The gravitational force between two objects of masses m₁ and m₂ is directly proportional to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**m₁ × m₂**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The gravitational force between two objects is governed by Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation.
 
• The formula for gravitational force is F = G * (m₁ * m₂) / r², where G is the gravitational constant.
 
• The force is directly proportional to the product of the masses of the two objects (m₁ and m₂).
 
• This means that if either mass increases, the gravitational force between them also increases.
 
• The gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the centers of the two masses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Constant (G)**

 
 
• G is a universal constant with a value of approximately 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N(m/kg)².
 
 
 
• It is a key component in the formula for calculating gravitational force.
 
• **Inverse Square Law**
 
 
• This law states that the force between two masses is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• This means that if the distance is doubled, the gravitational force becomes one-fourth.
 
 
 
• **Mass and Weight**
 
 
• Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is usually measured in kilograms.
 
• Weight is the force exerted by gravity on an object and is dependent on both the mass of the object and the gravitational field strength.
 
• Weight can be calculated using the formula Weight = Mass × Gravitational field strength.

questions.question: The HCF of the numbers 310, 208 and 180 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **HCF** of any set of numbers must divide the **difference** between any two of those numbers.

The difference between 208 and 180 is 28.

The factors of 28 are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, and 28.

Since 310 is not divisible by 4, the HCF cannot be 4, 14, or 28.

Since all three numbers (310, 208, and 180) are **even numbers**, they are divisible by 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 310, 208, and 180.

**Formula Used:**

**HCF** (Highest Common Factor) is the product of the **lowest powers** of all common prime factors.

**Calculations:**

Let us find the **prime factorisation** of each number:

⇒ 310 = 2 × 5 × 31

⇒ 208 = 2⁴ × 13

⇒ 180 = 2² × 3² × 5

Identify the common prime factors:

⇒ The only prime factor common to all three numbers is 2.

⇒ The lowest power of 2 among the factorisations is 2¹.

⇒ HCF = 2¹ = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. It is also referred to as the **Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)**.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest non-zero common multiple of two or more numbers.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is equal to the product of the two numbers: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be **co-prime** if their HCF is 1.</p

__
 
• The magnetic field produced by a current-carrying wire is directly proportional to the current flowing through the wire.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field decreases as the distance from the wire increases.
 
• The relationship between the magnetic field (B), current (I), and distance (r) is given by the Biot-Savart law and Ampère's circuital law.

• It states that if you point the thumb of your right hand in the direction of the current, your fingers will curl in the direction of the magnetic field.

questions.question: An order was placed for the supply of a carpet whose breadth was 6 m and whose length were 1.44 times the breadth. What is the cost of a carpet whose length and breadth are 40% more and 25% more respectively than the first carpet. [The cost of a carpet is Rs. 45 per sq m.]
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

New **Area** = Old **Area** × (1 + % increase in **length**) × (1 + % increase in **breadth**)

Old **Area** = 6 × (1.44 × 6) = 51.84 m²

New **Area** = 51.84 × 1.40 × 1.25 = 51.84 × 1.75 = 90.72 m²

Total **Cost** = 90.72 × 45 = ₹4082.40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4082.40.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First carpet **breadth** (B₁) = 6 m

First carpet **length** (L₁) = 1.44 × 6 = 8.64 m

Rate of **carpet** = ₹45 per sq m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3d7daf7606f501799b4a1728531936918024051fab661d0639de90ca1221c3b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Breadth** of second carpet (B₂) = 6 + (25% of 6) = 6 × 1.25 = 7.5 m

⇒ **Length** of second carpet (L₂) = 8.64 + (40% of 8.64) = 8.64 × 1.4 = 12.096 m

⇒ **Area** of second carpet = L₂ × B₂

⇒ **Area** = 12.096 × 7.5 = 90.72 m²

⇒ Total **Cost** = **Area** × Rate

⇒ Total **Cost** = 90.72 × 45

⇒ Total **Cost** = ₹4082.40

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4082.40.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of Rectangle

The total space occupied by a **rectangle** is given by the formula: Area = **Length** × **Breadth**.

Successive Percentage Increase

If two dimensions are increased by a% and b%, the resultant **area** increases by [a + b + (a×b)/100]%. In this case: 40 + 25 + (40×25)/100 = 75% total increase.

Unitary Method for Cost

Total **Cost** = (Total **Quantity**/**Area**) × (Rate per unit **Quantity**/**Area**).

questions.question: Simplify: (1 - sec² θ)(1 - sin θ)(1 + sin θ)(1 + cot² θ).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put a specific value for **θ** to solve quickly, let **θ = 45°**.

⇒ (1 − sec² 45°)(1 − sin 45°)(1 + sin 45°)(1 + cot² 45°)

⇒ (1 − 2)(1 − 1/√2)(1 + 1/√2)(1 + 1)

⇒ (−1) × (1 − 1/2) × 2 = (−1) × (1/2) × 2 = −1.

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (1 − sec² θ)(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)(1 + cot² θ)

**Formula Used:**

1. sec² θ − tan² θ = 1 ⇒ 1 − sec² θ = −tan² θ

2. (a − b)(a + b) = a² − b²

3. sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 ⇒ 1 − sin² θ = cos² θ

4. cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1 ⇒ 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0038cbc0f184f985c8552fe6e2565a75bdc862d49b6ed4d751f7bd10de23b0a9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ [(1 − sec² θ)] × [(1 − sin θ)(1 + sin θ)] × [1 + cot² θ]

⇒ [−tan² θ] × [1 − sin² θ] × [cosec² θ]

⇒ (−tan² θ) × (cos² θ) × (cosec² θ)

⇒ (−sin² θ / cos² θ) × (cos² θ) × (1 / sin² θ)

⇒ −sin² θ × (1 / sin² θ)

⇒ −1

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

Standard identities used in trigonometry: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ.

Reciprocal Relations

Important reciprocals: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ, cot θ = cos θ / sin θ, and sin θ × cosec θ = 1.

Algebraic Conjugates

The product of (1 − sin θ) and (1 + sin θ) is 1 − sin² θ, which simplifies to cos² θ.</p

questions.question: If a : b = 3 : 2 and b : c = 4 : 5 , then a : b : c = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Write the **ratios** as: a : b = 3 : 2 and b : c = 4 : 5.

Multiply the first ratio by 2 to make the **common term** 'b' equal in both cases (LCM of 2 and 4 is 4).

a : b = (3 × 2) : (2 × 2) = 6 : 4.

Now, combine the values directly: a = 6, b = 4, and c = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 4 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio a : b = 3 : 2

Ratio b : c = 4 : 5

**Formula Used:**

To find the **combined ratio** a : b : c, the value of the common variable 'b' must be made identical in both given ratios by using its **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e72a936f93c49cec1f13b3fc643c030f0840f63be5d0386d8ee908e95074c41.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ a/b = 3/2

⇒ b/c = 4/5

⇒ To equate 'b', find **LCM** of 2 and 4 = 4.

⇒ Multiply a/b by 2/2: (3 × 2) / (2 × 2) = 6/4

⇒ Now, a = 6, b = 4

⇒ From second ratio, b = 4, c = 5

⇒ a : b : c = 6 : 4 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 6 : 4 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together (antecedent with antecedent and consequent with consequent), it is called a **compound ratio**. For a : b and c : d, it is (a × c) : (b × d).

Duplicate Ratio

The **duplicate ratio** of a : b is a² : b². Similarly, the **sub-duplicate ratio** is √a : √b.

Proportion Rule

If four quantities a, b, c, d are in **proportion** (a : b = c : d), then the product of extremes equals the product of means: a × d = b × c.</p

questions.question: Which of the following types of reaction represents formation of slaked lime from calcium oxide and water?

The correct answer is __**Combination reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a combination reaction, two or more substances combine to form a single product.
 
• The formation of slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) from calcium oxide and water is a classic example of a combination reaction.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.
 
• This type of reaction is exothermic, meaning it releases heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposition reaction**

 
 
• This type of reaction involves a single compound breaking down into two or more simpler substances.
 
• An example of a decomposition reaction is the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation reaction**
 
 
• In a precipitation reaction, two solutions react to form an insoluble solid, known as the precipitate.
 
• An example is the reaction between silver nitrate and sodium chloride to form silver chloride precipitate.
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction**
 
 
• This type of reaction involves an element displacing another element in a compound, forming a new compound.
 
• An example is the reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid, where zinc displaces hydrogen to form zinc chloride and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of osmosis?

options.text: Absorption of water by plant roots
Movement of O₂ and CO₂ in and out of the living cell
Swelling of raisins when soaked in water
Gaining of water by unicellular fresh water organisms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Movement of O₂ and CO₂ in and out of the living cell**__.

__**Note**__**:**** **According to the official answer key, the given answer is **Option 4 **but in actual the correct answer would be **Option 2** because movement of O₂ and CO₂ in and out of living cells is not an example of osmosis; it occurs through the process of diffusion and gaining of water by unicellular freshwater organisms happens through osmosis as water enters the organism from the surrounding environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Osmosis is the process of water molecules moving across a semipermeable membrane from an area of lower solute concentration to an area of higher solute concentration.
 
• Absorption of water by plant roots is an example of osmosis, as water moves from the soil (lower solute concentration) into the roots (higher solute concentration).
 
• Swelling of raisins when soaked in water occurs due to osmosis, where water moves into the raisins causing them to swell.
 
• Gaining of water by unicellular freshwater organisms happens through osmosis as water enters the organism from the surrounding environment.
 
• Movement of O₂ and CO₂ in and out of living cells is not an example of osmosis; it occurs through the process of diffusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffusion**

 
 
• Diffusion is the movement of molecules from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
 
• It does not require a semipermeable membrane and can involve various types of molecules including gases and small solutes.
 
 
 
• **Active Transport**
 
 
• Active transport is the movement of molecules against their concentration gradient, requiring energy in the form of ATP.
 
• This process is essential for maintaining concentration gradients of ions across cell membranes.
 
 
 
• **Facilitated Diffusion**
 
 
• Facilitated diffusion is a type of passive transport that involves the use of carrier proteins to move molecules across a cell membrane.
 
• It is important for the transport of substances that cannot diffuse freely across the membrane.

questions.question: 8 men and 12 women can build a wall in 10 days. 6 men and 8 women can build the same wall in 14 days. How long will take for 2 women and 1 man to build it together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate work: 10(8M + 12W) = 14(6M + 8W) ⇒ 80M + 120W = 84M + 112W.

Efficiency ratio: **4M = 8W** ⇒ **1 Man = 2 Women**.

Total work (in women units) = (8 × 2 + 12) × 10 = **280 units**.

Required efficiency (2W + 1M) = 2 + 2 = **4 units/day**.

Time taken = 280 ÷ 4 = **70 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 8 men and 12 women in **10 days**; 6 men and 8 women in **14 days**.

**Formula:** Total Work = (Number of people × Efficiency) × Time

 
 

 **Group**
 **Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 8M + 12W
 10
 70
 70 ÷ 10 = 7
 
 

 6M + 8W
 14
 70 ÷ 14 = 5
 
 

⇒ 8M + 12W = 7 ......(i)

⇒ 6M + 8W = 5 ......(ii)

Multiply eq(i) by 2 and eq(ii) by 3 to eliminate W:

⇒ 16M + 24W = 14

⇒ 18M + 24W = 15

Subtracting gives: 2M = 1 ⇒ **Efficiency of 1 Man = 0.5**

Substitute M in eq(ii): 6(0.5) + 8W = 5 ⇒ 3 + 8W = 5 ⇒ 8W = 2 ⇒ **Efficiency of 1 Woman = 0.25**

Efficiency of 2 women and 1 man = 2(0.25) + 0.5 = **1 unit/day**.

Time taken = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 70 ÷ 1 = **70 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Concept

The total work is always constant for a given task and is expressed as M₁D₁H₁ = M₂D₂H₂ where M is the number of workers, D is days, and H is hours.

Work and Efficiency

Time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to efficiency: Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency.

Pipes and Cisterns

A similar concept where the rate of filling or emptying a tank follows the same logic as the efficiency of men and women.</p

• C₂H₄, also known as ethene, is an unsaturated hydrocarbon because it contains a carbon-carbon double bond.
 
• Compounds like C₂H₆ (ethane) and C₃H₈ (propane) are saturated hydrocarbons, meaning they only have single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons are more reactive than saturated hydrocarbons due to the presence of double or triple bonds.

questions.question: A car moving along a straight path slows down and stops. The car is under which type of motion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-uniform motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A car slowing down and eventually stopping is an example of **non-uniform motion**, where the speed of the car changes over time.
 
• In non-uniform motion, the velocity of the object is not constant, and there is an acceleration or deceleration involved.
 
• This type of motion can be described by the change in speed and direction, indicating a varying rate of displacement.
 
• Non-uniform motion is often analyzed using kinematic equations that take into account initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration, and time.
 
• Examples of non-uniform motion include a car braking to a stop, a ball rolling down a hill, or a plane taking off and landing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uniform Motion**

 
 
• In uniform motion, an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time without changing its speed or direction.
 
• Examples include a car cruising at a constant speed on a straight road or the Earth orbiting the Sun at a constant speed.
 
 
 
• **Circular Motion**
 
 
• This type of motion occurs when an object moves along a circular path at a constant or varying speed.
 
• Examples include the rotation of a fan blade or a satellite orbiting a planet.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Motion**
 
 
• Periodic motion is characterized by the repetition of motion at regular time intervals.
 
• Examples include the swinging of a pendulum or the oscillation of a spring.

questions.question: In a row of 34 students facing North, Jignesh is 12th from the right end. If Kamlesh is 7th to the left of Jignesh, what is Kamlesh's position from the left end of the line?
questions.solution:
Given: 

Number of students in the row = 34

Jignesh's position from the right end = 12th

Kamlesh is 7th to the left of Jignesh

So, Kamlesh's position from the right end = Jignesh's position from the right end + 7

Kamlesh's position from the right end = 12 + 7 = 19

To find Kamlesh's position from the left end:

Kamlesh's position from the left end = Total number of students - Kamlesh's position from the right end + 1

Kamlesh's position from the left end = 34 - 19 + 1 = 16

Thus, Kamlesh's position from the left end is **"16th".**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question: The nature of an image formed by a concave mirror when an object is kept at the position between the principal focus and the pole of the mirror is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**virtual and erect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed between the principal focus (F) and the pole (P) of a concave mirror, the image formed is virtual and erect.
 
• The image appears on the same side of the mirror as the object.
 
• This virtual image is enlarged compared to the actual object.
 
• Concave mirrors are also known as converging mirrors as they converge light rays that are incident parallel to the principal axis.
 
• Such mirrors are commonly used in applications like shaving mirrors, makeup mirrors, and certain optical instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirrors**

 
 
• Convex mirrors, or diverging mirrors, form virtual, diminished, and erect images regardless of the position of the object.
 
• They are commonly used in vehicles as rear-view mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Plane Mirrors**
 
 
• Plane mirrors form virtual, erect images that are the same size as the object.
 
• The image formed is laterally inverted.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Mirrors**
 
 
• Concave mirrors are used in telescopes, headlights, and solar furnaces due to their converging properties.
 
• Convex mirrors are used in security and safety applications due to their wide field of view.

questions.question: A dishonest dealer professes to sell goods at the cost price, but uses a false weight of 900 grams instead of a kg. His gain percentage is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Gain %** = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100

Here, **True Value** = 1000 g and **Error** = 1000 − 900 = 100 g.

Gain % = [100 ÷ (1000 − 100)] × 100 = (100 ÷ 900) × 100

Gain % = 100 ÷ 9 = 11 1/9 %

**∴ The correct answer is 11 1/9 %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**True Weight** = 1 kg = 1000 g

**False Weight** used by dealer = 900 g

**Selling Price (SP)** = Cost Price (CP) of 1000 g

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/440d052ed517854e05f9150036b6d9ee755e8b3e960aba1a8b200d99a1a99eac.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 g of goods be ₹1.

⇒ CP of 1000 g (True weight) = ₹1000.

⇒ The dealer sells 900 g for the price of 1000 g.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** of 900 g = ₹1000.

⇒ **Actual CP** of 900 g for the dealer = ₹900.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = ₹1000 − ₹900 = ₹100.

⇒ Profit % = (100 ÷ 900) × 100

questions.question: The sum of a two-digit number and the number obtained by reversing the digits is 99. If the digits of the number differ by 7, then the two-digit number can be:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of digits (x + y) = **Total Sum ÷ 11** ⇒ 99 ÷ 11 = **9**.

Difference of digits (x − y) is given as **7**.

To find the larger digit (x): (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (9 + 7) ÷ 2 = **8**.

To find the smaller digit (y): (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (9 − 7) ÷ 2 = **1**.

Possible numbers are **81** or **18**. From the options, **81** is the correct one.

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of a **two-digit number** and its **reverse** is 99. The **digits differ** by 7.

**Formula Used:** Let a two-digit number be 10x + y, where x is the **tens digit** and y is the **units digit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16c81f2dff5155ba16bf44ca2381eaca546a018c4f045fca1c03f9a67466b5d2.png] 

⇒ (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 99

⇒ 11x + 11y = 99

⇒ x + y = 9 ... (Eq. 1)

⇒ Case 1: x − y = 7 ... (Eq. 2)

⇒ Adding Eq. 1 and Eq. 2: 2x = 16 ⇒ **x = 8**

⇒ Substituting x in Eq. 1: 8 + y = 9 ⇒ **y = 1**

⇒ The number is 10(8) + 1 = **81**.

⇒ Case 2: y − x = 7 ⇒ y = 8, x = 1. Number = 18 (not in options).

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 11

The sum of any two-digit number and its reverse is always a multiple of 11. Specifically, (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 11(x + y).

Divisibility by 9

The difference between a two-digit number and its reverse is always a multiple of 9. Specifically, (10x + y) − (10y + x) = 9(x − y).

Expanded Notation

Any number can be expressed in terms of its place values. For a three-digit number 'abc', the value is 100a + 10b + c.</p

questions.question: Find the perimeter of a rhombus whose diagonals are of lengths 6 cm and 8 cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a **rhombus**, the side (a) and **diagonals** (d₁, d₂) are related by: a = ½ √(d₁² + d₂²)

Given d₁ = 6 cm and d₂ = 8 cm, the side a = ½ √(6² + 8²) = ½ √(36 + 64) = ½ √100 = 5 cm.

**Perimeter** = 4 × side = 4 × 5 = 20 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first diagonal (d₁) = 6 cm

Length of second diagonal (d₂) = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

Diagonals of a **rhombus** bisect each other at 90°. Using **Pythagoras Theorem** in the resulting right-angled triangles:

Side² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

Perimeter = 4 × side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/900991ff3798ab33f49485439d3eb03e4d12ce88c3037ec4a5be512d4bd29628.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Half of first diagonal = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Half of second diagonal = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm

⇒ Side² = 3² + 4²

⇒ Side² = 9 + 16 = 25

⇒ Side = √25 = 5 cm

⇒ Perimeter of Rhombus = 4 × 5 = 20 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rhombus

The area is calculated using the product of the diagonals: Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂.

Properties of a Rhombus

All four sides are equal in length, and diagonals bisect each other at **right angles** (90°).

Pythagorean Triplet

The values (3, 4, 5) form a standard **Pythagorean triplet**, making calculations faster for right-angled triangles.</p

questions.question: Two trains of equal length, running at the speeds of 60 km/h and 40 km/h, take 50 seconds to cross each other while they are running in the same direction. What time will they take to cross each other if they are running in opposite directions?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Since the **Total Distance** (sum of train lengths) remains constant in both cases, the **Time** taken is inversely proportional to the **Relative Speed**.

Relative speed in **Same Direction** (S₁ − S₂) = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h

Relative speed in **Opposite Direction** (S₁ + S₂) = 60 + 40 = 100 km/h

Required Time = 50 sec × (20 / 100) = 50 × 1/5 = 10 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 10 sec.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = 60 km/h, Speed of Train 2 (S₂) = 40 km/h

Time to cross in **Same Direction** = 50 sec

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time | Relative Speed (Same) = S₁ − S₂ | Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50409378cf8b8ca31c774d157ffdeed45f9a2610df447668865e0ff63a38a3b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed (Same) = (60 − 40) × 5/18 m/s = 20 × 5/18 = 50/9 m/s

⇒ Total Distance (D) = Relative Speed (Same) × Time = (50/9) × 50 = 2500/9 meters

⇒ Relative Speed (Opposite) = (60 + 40) × 5/18 m/s = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s

⇒ Time (Opposite) = Total Distance / Relative Speed (Opposite)

⇒ Time (Opposite) = (2500/9) / (250/9) = 2500 / 250 = 10 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 10 sec.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (u − v). When they move in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Time Rule

The distance covered when two trains cross each other is always equal to the sum of the lengths of the two trains (L₁ + L₂).</p

questions.question: A solution contains 40 g of common salt in 320 g of water. What is the concentration of the solution in terms of mass by mass percentage?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• To determine the concentration of a solution in terms of mass by mass percentage, you need to divide the mass of the solute (common salt) by the total mass of the solution.
 
• The total mass of the solution is the sum of the mass of the solute and the solvent (water).
 
• In this case, the mass of the solute (common salt) is 40 g and the mass of the solvent (water) is 320 g.
 
• The total mass of the solution = 40 g + 320 g = 360 g.
 
• Mass by mass percentage = (Mass of solute / Total mass of solution) x 100 = (40 g / 360 g) x 100 = 11.11%.

• **Mass by volume percentage**

 
 
• This is another common way to express the concentration of a solution, where the mass of the solute is divided by the volume of the solution, and the result is multiplied by 100.
 
 
 
• **Molarity**
 
 
• Molarity is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution. It is a commonly used unit for expressing the concentration of a solution in chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Molality**
 
 
• Molality is the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent. This unit is useful in various chemical calculations, particularly when dealing with temperature changes.

questions.question: By how much is 80% of 40 greater than (4)/(5) of 25?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

80% of 40 and (4/5) of 25

**Formula Used:**

Percentage of a number = (Percentage × Number) / 100

Fraction of a number = (Fraction × Number)

**Calculation:**

80% of 40 = (80 × 40) / 100 = 3200 / 100 = 32

Now, (4/5) of 25

⇒ (4/5) × 25 = 4 × 5 = 20

Difference

⇒ 32 - 20 = 12

**The difference is 12.**

questions.question: Which of the following substances can move across the cell membrane by diffusion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxygen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Diffusion is a passive transport mechanism where substances move from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
 
• Oxygen is a small, nonpolar molecule that can easily diffuse across the cell membrane without the need for transport proteins.
 
• Nucleic acids, proteins, and starch are large molecules that cannot pass through the cell membrane by simple diffusion.
 
• The cell membrane is selectively permeable, allowing only certain molecules to pass through while blocking others.
 
• Oxygen diffusion is crucial for cellular respiration, a process that generates ATP, the energy currency of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Facilitated Diffusion**

 
 
• This process involves the use of transport proteins to move substances across the cell membrane.
 
• It is used for molecules that cannot diffuse directly through the lipid bilayer, such as glucose and amino acids.
 
 
 
• **Active Transport**
 
 
• Active transport requires energy in the form of ATP to move substances against their concentration gradient.
 
• This process involves transport proteins such as pumps and is essential for maintaining cellular homeostasis.
 
 
 
• **Endocytosis and Exocytosis**
 
 
• These are processes used by cells to transport large molecules or particles across the cell membrane.
 
• Endocytosis involves the engulfing of substances into the cell, while exocytosis involves the expulsion of substances from the cell.
